rulings.Case Title: IBARRA PROFESSIONAL LAW CORPORATION VS. DING HE MINING HOLDINGS LIMITED ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion To: (1) Compel Defendant Paulo Zhou Heng Gu To Answer Judgment Debtor Interrogatories; And (2) For Monetary Sanctions Against Defendant In Having To File The Motion To Compel
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Line 4, PLAINTIFF IBARRA PROFESSIONAL LAW CORPORATION's Motion To: (1) Compel Defendant Paulo Zhou Heng Gu To Answer Judgment Debtor Interrogatories; And (2) For Monetary Sanctions Against Defendant In Having To File The Motion To Compel. Judgment creditor Ibarra Professional Law Corporation's motion to compel judgment debtor Paulo Gu to serve further responses to judgment enforcement interrogatories and for monetary sanctions is denied as moot as to interrogatories 1-13, granted as to interrogatories 14-2, and granted in part as to monetary sanctions. Gu's substantive responses to interrogatories 1-13 moot this motion as to those interrogatories. If Ibarra Corp. believes any of those responses are deficient, it will need to engage in further meet and confer and, if the issues are not resolved by the meet and confer, file another motion. Gu's most recent objections based on the Fifth Amendment to interrogatories 14-22 lack merit. Like Mr. Troy in Troy v. Superior Court (1986) 186 Cal. App. 3d 1006, 1013, Gu's fear that he may be subjected to criminal prosecution is based on speculation and not the existence of "real danger" that is required for the valid invocation of the Fifth Amendment. Gu must serve verified code-complaint further supplemental responses without objections to interrogatories 14-22 no later than August 3, 2026. Gu's original responses to the interrogatories and his belated service of further responses lack substantial justification requiring an award of monetary sanctions against him. No later than September 30, 2026 Gu must pay reasonable monetary sanctions of $3,083.75 to Ibarra Corp. rulings.Case Title: CHARLES LI VS. MEI LING FANG ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Set Aside Default Judgment
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Line 17, DEFENDANT SHUZHEN TU's Motion To Set Aside Default Judgment. (Complete tentative ruling emailed to the parties). The motion of defendants Shuhen Tu, Meiling Fang, Vi Tran and Demas Yan to set aside the default judgment filed April 29, 2026 is denied. The sole bases argued by defendants to set aside the judgment is that the judgment is a "void judgment" per CCP 473(d) because 1) plaintiff Charles Li lacked standing to bring a wrongful foreclosure lawsuit and 2) Li asserted facts at the default judgment hearing that were from those included in his complaint and thus he made a "de facto amendment" of his complaint violating defendants' due process rights. Assuming without deciding that Li lacked standing as contended by defendants and he asserted facts at the default judgment hearing materially different from those in his complaint, the judgment is not void and may not be set aside per 473(d). rulings.Case Title: JITU CURRY ET AL VS. SANDBOX VR, INC., ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Tax Costs; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities; Declaration Of Andrew Williams, Esq.
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Line 5, PLAINTIFF JITU CURRY, GILBERT DORSEY's Motion To Tax Costs. Plaintiffs Jitu Curry and Gilbert Dorsey's motion to tax costs is denied. The sole basis for the motion is the assertion that the memorandum of costs filed by defendant Sandbox VR, Inc. was untimely filed. To the contrary, the memorandum of costs was arguably prematurely filed since no judgment has yet been entered and, per CRC 3.1700(a)(1) it is the entry of judgment that triggers the deadline to file a memorandum of costs. rulings.Case Title: POCKET ENTERTAINMENT SERVICES LLC VS. MOZILLA CORPORATION
rulings.Calendar Matter: Motion To Seal Re Plaintiffs Ex Parte Application For: (1) A Temporary Restraining Order; And (2) An Order To Show Cause Why Preliminary Injunction Should Not Issue
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Wednesday, August 12, 2026, Line 16, DEFENDANT MOZILLA CORPORATION's Motion To Seal Re Plaintiffs Ex Parte Application For: (1) A Temporary Restraining Order; And (2) An Order To Show Cause Why Preliminary Injunction Should Not Issue. Defendant Mozilla Corporation's motion to seal certain information filed conditionally under seal on July 7, 2026 is denied. Assuming without deciding that there is an overriding interest of abiding by contractual confidentiality provisions and that overriding interest supports sealing court records, Mozilla has not shown by the required "facts" (CRC 2.551(b)(1)) that a substantial probability exists that the overriding interest will be substantially prejudiced if the identity of the third-party purchaser of pocket.com is not sealed. The declaration of Mozilla's general counsel is wholly conclusory and conjectural on that critical point. The only materials filed conditionally under seal that are sought to be sealed are unredacted versions of the ex parte application and the Declaration of Neha Anderson without exhibits filed July 7, 2026. The unredacted versions of those documents will now be filed without sealing. The court does not have exhibits H, J and Q to the Anderson Declaration, so the portion of this motion directed to those exhibits is off calendar. While the court does have an unredacted version of the proposed order that was lodged on July 7, 2026, that document. like all proposed orders that do not become orders of the court, has not nor will it ever be filed and is maintained and will remain in a file that is not available to the public, so the portion of this motion directed to the proposed order is also off calendar.
